summary: Catherine Bell (1954–2008) worked in religious studies and sinology. She studied at the University of Chicago under Joseph Mitsuo Kitagawa (~1976–1983) and served as the Bernard J. Hanley Professor of Religious Studies at Santa Clara University (1985–2008).

Catherine Elaine Prueitt is a scholar of indology, philosophy, and religious studies. She earned her BA from the University of Rochester (completed 2007) and her PhD from Emory University (completed 2016), studying under doctoral supervisor John D. Dunne and teacher Laurie L. Patton.

Catherine Ludvik specializes in religious studies, japanology, and indology. She earned her PhD from the University of Toronto (completed 2001) under David Waterhouse, Antonino Forte, Yuko Matsuda, and Werner Knobl. She held posts at the Italian School of East Asian Studies and Hanazono University.
Cathy Cantwell specializes in tibetology and buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Kent (~1984–1989) and held a post at the University of Oxford in 2002.

Cecil Bendall (1856–1906) was a scholar of indology and buddhist studies who studied at Oxford and Cambridge, under Edward Byles Cowell and Theodor Benfey. He held posts at the British Museum, University College London, and Cambridge, where he was Professor of Sanskrit.

Cecil Y. Lang (1920–2003) studied at Duke University (~1937–1941). He held positions at Yale University (~1949–1951), the University of Chicago (~1965–1970), and the University of Virginia, where he was Professor of English (~1970–1991).

Chagdud Tulku Rinpoche (1930–2002) was a figure in buddhist studies and tibetology. He studied under Delog Dawa Drolma, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and Dudjom Rinpoche, and he taught Albion Moonlight Butters.

Chaisit Suwanvarangkul is a scholar of buddhist studies and philosophy. He conducted research at Kyoto University and the University of Delhi, and he served as a Lecturer in Buddhist Studies at the University of Otago (attested 2015).

Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad specializes in philosophy, religious studies, and indology. After earning a doctorate at the University of Oxford, he held posts at Clare Hall, Cambridge, Trinity College, Oxford, the National University of Singapore, and Lancaster University, where he was Professor (attested 2007–2012).

Chamnong Adivadhanasit is a scholar of religious and buddhist studies. He earned a BA at Chulalongkorn University, where he was a part-time instructor (attested 2012), and served as a professor in the Faculty of Social Science at Kasetsart University (attested 2012).
Champa Thupten Zongtse specializes in tibetology and buddhist studies. He held posts at the University of Göttingen, where he was attested in 1991 and served as a lecturer in 2009.

Chandrabhal Tripathi (1929–1996) was an indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt (~1957–1960). He held posts at Göttingen, Cologne, Humboldt University of Berlin (attested 1985), and the Free University of Berlin (~1977–1994).
Chang-geun Hwang is a scholar of buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 2000, studying under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Minoru Kiyota, and Morten Schlütter.

Changhwan Park is a scholar of buddhist studies, indology, and philosophy. He studied at Otani University and earned a PhD from UC Berkeley under Alexander von Rospatt and Noritoshi Aramaki. He served as a professor at Geumgang University (attested 2013–2017).

Chanju Mun is a buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (2001–2002) and earned a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2002). His supervisors and teachers included Charles Hallisey, Masahiro Shimoda, Morten Schlütter, Gudrun Bühnemann, and John D. Dunne.

Charlene Elizabeth Makley specializes in tibetology and anthropology. She earned her PhD from the University of Michigan (completed 1999) under Norma Diamond and Roy Rappaport, and she became an associate professor of anthropology at Reed College.

Charles A. Moore (1901–1967) was a philosopher who studied at Yale University (~1926–1932). He served as a professor at the University of Hawaii (~1936–1967) and edited Philosophy East and West (~1951–1967).

Charles B. Jones works in buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Virginia under Paul Groner in 1996, later becoming an associate professor and associate dean at the Catholic University of America (attested 2016–2019).

Charles D. Orzech works in religious studies, sinology, and buddhist studies. He completed his dissertation at the University of Chicago, served as chair of Religious Studies at UNC Greensboro (attested 1998–2006), and was a fellow at the National Humanities Center (2009–2010).

Charles Duroiselle (1871–1951) was a scholar in archaeology, buddhist studies, and indology. He held posts at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1905–1916), the University of Yangon (~1908–1919), the Archaeological Survey of India (1919, 1936), and the Department of Archaeology (1936).
